reviewer.actual_effort: Read in full: current.json, current-xml.xml (both parts, lines 1-178), page-audits.json, guideline-excerpts.md, english-rest-resolutions.json and english-routing-proof.xml. Looked at the original full-page English images s175, s183, s185 and s187 at their displayed resolution (1208x2000, from 1368x2264) and compared them word by word with the encoded English. Did not enlarge any crops. Did not open s177, s179 or s181; for those pages I relied on the earlier full-page audit (claude-opus-5-5, low effort, no magnification). Did not run any validators, tests or exports.

scope: English source accuracy and English encoding against the guidelines for: torah_vezot_hatorah, haftarah_before_blessing, haftarah_samuel_1, haftarah_after_blessings, haftarah_al_hatorah, shofar_ribbon_haolamim_banekha, shofar_yehi_ratzon, shofar_qera_satan. Also the correspondence boundaries the English shares with the Hebrew files. Hebrew wording, vowels, accents and fine marks were not reviewed and are not approved.

issues.problem: There are double spaces where text meets a conditional or milestone. This is whitespace only and doesn't change any wording, but a renderer that doesn't collapse whitespace would show two spaces.
issues.fix: Optional: tidy to a single space. No source change is needed.

remaining_source_questions: The English tei:head 'Prayer before the Shofar' matches the running head on s185 (the header line with page number 81 at both ends). The page body has no separate section heading. Please confirm that using a running title as the witness head is the project's convention when a section opens a page. The same running title appears on s187, where no head is encoded, which looks consistent. This doesn't affect the approval of the body text.

verified: s175 against the image: the body text of torah_vezot_hatorah, haftarah_before_blessing and haftarah_samuel_1 verses 1:1–1:4 'On' matches the print exactly, including 'supports it, is made happy', 'King of the World,' and 'Romathaim-Tsofim'. The italic rubrics 'After the reading, … one says:' and 'Blessing before the Haphtorah:' and the heading 'Haphtarah' match documentary_instructions. The printed citation '(1 Samuel, ch. 1—2 v. 10)' is encoded without its parentheses, which is the convention.

s183 against the image: haftarah_samuel_1 'man prevails.' and 2:10 match. The rubric 'Blessings after the Haphtorah:' matches. All four after-blessing paragraphs match, including 'centre', 'thine anointed', 'Holy Name' and 'Lord, shield of David.'. haftarah_al_hatorah matches, including the three printed parentheticals '(Sabbath day and this)', '(for holiness and rest)' and '(the Sabbath)'. Each is encoded as j:conditional type='marked' with the parentheses removed, which follows 'How an undecided scope is set off'. Each parenthetical's extent matches the corresponding Hebrew conditional (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם / לִקְדֻשָּׁה וְלִמְנוּחָה / הַשַּׁבָּת וְ), and all use the same holiday-aggregate condition shabbat=true. al_hatorah is one printed paragraph and is encoded as one tei:p with two prayer-parts (al and seal), and the seal boundary sits at 'Blessed art Thou' on both sides.

s183 italic direction: the page-audit finding of a missing instruction is resolved. english-routing-proof.xml shows it encoded in the English source index as a tei:note type='instruction' with the exact printed wording. The first sentence sits outside tei:seg type='optional-page-reference' and the Sabbath clause with the page reference sits inside it, using the edition-qualified yequm_purqan/scholars URN. There is no final period after '(p. 85)', matching the print. This follows 'Page references in a generated edition'.

s185 against the image: the ribbon_haolamim_banekha English matches word for word, including 'Shofar . . . I myself', 'before thee, O Lord' with a lowercase 'thee' as printed, and 'redeemer, Amen.'. The Psalm 47:6 and 19:15 seg/source spans have extents that match the Hebrew segs.

s187 against the image: the yehi_ratzon English matches, and the printed 'May it by Thy will' is emitted as tei:choice sic='by', corr='be' from the existing correction layer (no duplicate correction proposed). 'in compassion. Amen.' matches. qera_satan is one printed paragraph and is encoded as one tei:p with six seg/source verses whose wording and order match the print: Lamentations 3:56 and Psalms 119:160, 122, 162, 66, 108.

s177, s179 and s181 (not checked against images by me): the existing full-page audit found every body accounted for and no source findings. The 'Lo:d' on s181 is broken type, and the encoded 'Lord' is correct. The verse wording in current.json matches the encoded XML exactly. No resolutions entry affects these witnesses.

Milestone scopes follow rules 2 and 3 of 'URN scope': every bounded quotation is closed by verse and chapter terminators. In vezot_hatorah, the Numbers 9:23 verse-part 'al_pi' is closed by a bare verse-part terminator before the verse and chapter terminators. Every prayer-part is closed by a bare terminator before the paragraph or division ends.

haftarah_samuel_1: the canonical verse milestones samuel_1/1/1–1/28 and 2/1–2/10 are the same on the English and Hebrew sides. Only chapter 1 carries a chapter corresp, which matches complete_chapters. Chapter 2 has only a bare start, so it doesn't claim a partial chapter as the whole of samuel_1/2. Page breaks n=77–80 fall at the printed points: 'On|the day', 'drunk?|Remove', 'Lord|at Shiloh' and 'that|man prevails'.

Repeated-Scripture quotations (vezot_hatorah, ribbon, qera_satan) follow the established local-corresp occurrence convention, with the canonical reference held in seg/@source. I'm not asking for duplicate canonical corresp.

The alignment URNs (prayer-part, chapter, verse and verse-part corresp) are the same in each English and Hebrew pair, so the exact-URN join described under 'Alignment' gives one row per verse or part.
Instructions printed only in the Hebrew (תחנות לתוקע…, במחזורים נדפסת…, ואח״כ יאמר…) are scoped to the Hebrew witness only. No English text is supplied for them, as required.
limits: I didn't open the images for s177, s179 and s181. My approval of haftarah_samuel_1 verses 1:4–2:9 relies on the existing low-effort, unmagnified full-page audit.
I worked from full-page images at their displayed resolution and didn't make enlarged crops. Nothing I saw was ambiguous enough to need them.
No Hebrew source acceptance is implied. I compared the Hebrew files only to check shared boundaries, extents, conditions and URNs.
This is a source and markup audit only. I didn't run the validators, test_repeated_scripture_has_addressable_chapter_and_verse_context, validate_urn_references or any renderer or export.

I didn't check whether documentary_instructions torah_haft_heading_en, together with the witness tei:head 'Haphtarah', could print the heading twice. That is a payload and renderer question, outside this source review.
